Ford's Theatre, forever linked to the assassination of President Abraham Lincoln, has also become part of DC's haunted lore. items.text: The worst take of the NFL season has already arrived, and it's about Brock Purdy
items.article: The undefeated San Francisco 49ers have been lauded by virtually everyone after a perfect start to 2026. Everyone, that is, but one Denver radio program. After the San Francisco 49ers thoroughly beat down the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams in Week 1 in Australia and reeled two more convincing wins against the lowly Dolphins and Cardinals, you’d be hard-pressed to find anyone with anything negative to say about them. They’re one of five unbeatens left in the NFL and lay claim to the No. 1 spot in a whole bunch of prominent power rankings , despite having already run out of spots on injured reserve . Quarterback Brock Purdy is an early front-runner for MVP with nine touchdowns and just one interception, leading arguably the best offense in football. items.article: The mint flavor of San Francisco's favorite It's-It ice cream cookie sandwiches has changed color. A major change has come for San Francisco’s beloved It’s-It ice cream sandwiches. The mint flavor of the ice cream cookie sandwich , once an ostentatiously loud shade of green, has changed color, as first spotted by the San Francisco Chronicle. (The Chronicle and SFGATE are both owned by Hearst but have separate newsrooms.) An SFGATE editor bought a box at Andronico’s and confirmed the breaking news — the bright, toothpaste-green ice cream had been drained of color, with a far more muted, pale pastel green in its place. Where the shade once screamed “GREEN!” at the top of its lungs, now, it only whispered. Curiously, though, It’s-It has mostly kept the change quiet. Despite SFGATE’s repeated attempts this week to reach the Burlingame-based company for comment, It’s-It never got back to us. The company has not released any statement announcing the change to its customers, and photos of the mint ice cream sandwich on its website remain the same , advertising the old seafoam green color instead of the new, lighter shade. It’s-It President Charles Shamieh did speak with the Chronicle, telling the outlet that It’s-It made the change due to U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. items.article: Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’ The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life. Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers. “I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push,” Machchhar told Modi in a video call on Friday. “I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realised that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives.” His Omani co-pilot apparently stabbed him and set the plane on a steep descent, with the aircraft plummeting about 17,000 feet in the span of a minute. While still being attacked, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter, subdue the attacker and ultimately stabilise the plane. The full circumstances of the attack are still under investigation, but a relief crew on the flight helped land the plane safely in Tabouk, north-west Saudi Arabia . items.text: After losing 25kg in my fifties, my wrinkled face looked like it was melting. Now strangers say I look two decades younger after a five-step cosmetic overhaul
items.article: When Susan Beach looked in the mirror after losing more than four stone, she expected to feel delighted by the woman staring back at her. Published: 17:05, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 17:18, 2 October 2026 The mother-of-two and realtor from Rochester, New York, had transformed her body after deciding to overhaul her lifestyle during the Covid-19 lockdown . The weight had steadily fallen away and Susan had finally achieved the figure she had wanted for years. But there was one part of her transformation she hadn't anticipated. Her face, she says, appeared to be 'melting'. As she lost weight, the skin around her cheeks and jaw became loose and droopy, while lines and wrinkles she had barely noticed before seemed suddenly more pronounced.
